findings.reason: a node landing §2 produces the reader in `served_code.py`, so the gate that consumes this plan's evidence looks for a `reckon/reach.py` that never appears and its evidence requirement goes unmet.
findings.text: §2 delivers the reachability reader in `reckon/served_code.py`, but the plan names gate `g-tcirbn-reach-instrument` as its one downstream consumer and that gate's measure is "`reckon/reach.py` returns the production modules one import away from a named path" (`the-codebase-is-reviewed-between-nodes.html:278`), a module §2 never names and that does not exist at this revision

findings.reason: as written the node cannot satisfy its own done-when without editing a file its scope excludes, so §3 must widen its write scope to the importing test or preserve `refusal_census`.
findings.text: §3 deletes `reckon/crew/context_budget.py` and scopes its test edits to "the test files whose only subject is a deleted module", but `tests/test_routing_surface.py:14` imports `context_budget` and lines 731–771 exercise `context_budget.refusal_census`; that file's subject is the routing surface, so it lies outside §3's write scope, yet §3's done-when requires `grep -rn context_budget reckon/ tests/ skills/` to return no hit and "the tests importing the touched modules" to pass

findings.reason: a worker following §4 literally cannot make `--help` exit 0 for two of the three modules, so the section must either describe adding an entry point each script needs or drop the `--help` measure.
findings.text: §4's done-when requires each moved module to run from `scripts/census/` with `--help`, but the deliverable describes only a move ("They move to scripts/census/ as standalone scripts"), and `reckon/crew/carryover_census.py` and `reckon/crew/pace_replay.py` carry no `__main__` guard and no argument parser (only `death_census.py` has a `__main__` calling `main()`), which §1 itself notes ("three of them carry a __main__ guard", none of them these two)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol, line, plan href and the consumer gate resolve (`reckon/served_code.py` `_ModuleIndex`/`_module_name`/`_module_file`/`_import_targets`/`_used_definitions` at 180/194/201/213/405; `reckon/velocity.py:428`; `reckon/interface_counts.py:74`; `budget.py:2651`; `routing.py:3533`; the three `docs/plans/*.html` targets; gate `g-tcirbn-reach-instrument` at `the-codebase-is-reviewed-between-nodes.html:278`), with extensionless hrefs resolved as `<path>.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §2, §3 and §4 names a declared negative control (extra unreached module fails the ratchet; restored call site makes the grep non-empty; a left-behind old import fails collection) with a measurable positive.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the sections start from the durable `~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/health-review-1010/health-reachability/` tree and log gates to the run manifest, not a session or node-local scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols are mechanism-named (`tests/test_reach_graph.py`, `tests/test_every_module_is_reached.py`, the reached set and `neighbourhood`); no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach code and no changelog prose appears.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — §3 deletes a module a non-scoped test still imports, and §4's `--help` measure is not produced by a plain move.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 is the reach instrument plus its ratchet guard, §3 is deletion of unowned unreached code, §4 is relocation of three one-off census modules; each closes on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the plan's declared consumer gate `g-tcirbn-reach-instrument` requires `reckon/reach.py`, but §2 delivers the reachability reader in `reckon/served_code.py`.
